scope: Relation-level coverage of the current field-only backlog; this report classifies research history and does not infer historical relationships.

research.note: The Chapel overview paper's primary-influence list (C, Modula, Fortran, C++, Java, C#, CLU, Scala, ML, Perl, Matlab) does not include Ada.
research.reopenWhen: Chapel's own material lists Ada as an overall design influence.

research.note: Wirth-family continuity and later Modula documentation were not treated as proof of a direct ALGOL 60 design edge; no qualifying direct statement was secured in this batch.
research.reopenWhen: A Modula primary report or author account explicitly identifies a concrete ALGOL 60 design input.

research.note: The official Oberon report is useful for Oberon’s own specification, but this batch did not obtain a direct ALGOL 60 design-source statement; intervening Modula history is not collapsed into a direct edge.
research.reopenWhen: An Oberon or Wirth primary source explicitly identifies ALGOL 60 as a concrete design input rather than only a family background.

research.note: Jule's design mission page states C/C++ only as a first-class interoperability goal and compile target, not as an overall design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Jule primary documentation states C as a design influence rather than interoperability.

research.note: Mojo's official documentation discusses lessons from other languages (e.g. Swift, C++, Rust, Zig) but does not list C as a design influence; scope is a missing listed influence, not proof of absence.
research.reopenWhen: Modular documentation lists C as a Mojo design influence.

research.note: Speedie documentation only notes C-library integration and performance comparison, not C as an overall design source.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states C as an overall design influence.

research.note: The Wa README describes a WebAssembly-oriented design goal but states no C design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Wa's own documentation states C as an overall design influence.

research.note: Jule's design mission page states C/C++ only as a first-class interoperability goal and compile target, not as an overall design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Jule primary documentation states C/C++ as a design influence rather than interoperability.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no C++ design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states C++ as an overall design influence.

research.note: Speedie documentation only compares against idiomatic C++ performance and notes C-library integration; it does not state C++ as an overall design source.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states C++ as an overall design influence.

research.note: The wa-lang README describes a WebAssembly-oriented design goal but does not state C++ as a design-influence source.
research.reopenWhen: wa-lang primary documentation states C++ as a design influence.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no C# design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states C# as an overall design influence.

research.note: Balgol history describes it as "an early dialect of the Algol-58 language"; the compiler focus "shifted from FORTRAN to Algol-58", so FORTRAN is not its design source.
research.reopenWhen: A primary source that states FORTRAN as an overall design influence on BALGOL is obtained.

research.note: MINI-EXPLOR is described as "A FORTRAN-Coded Version of the EXPLOR Language": FORTRAN is the implementation language, not the design source of EXPLOR.
research.reopenWhen: A primary source that states FORTRAN as an overall design influence on EXPLOR is obtained.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no Fortran design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states Fortran as an overall design influence.

research.note: The Wa README describes a WebAssembly-oriented design goal but states no Go design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Wa's own documentation states Go as an overall design influence.

research.note: Amber's official README and docs describe a language compiled to Bash and state no JavaScript design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Amber's official material states JavaScript as an overall design influence.

research.note: Scroll's site presents the language for scientific writing and lists no design influences.
research.reopenWhen: Scroll's own documentation states JavaScript as an overall design influence.

research.note: Speedie's README references JavaScript only as a negative comparison ("Doesn't infantilise you like Javascript or Java"), not as a design source.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states JavaScript as an overall design influence.

research.note: Lil's documentation does not name Lua among its stated influences.
research.reopenWhen: Lil's own documentation states Lua as an overall design influence.

research.note: Speedie's documentation does not name Lua as a design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states Lua as an overall design influence.

research.note: MLscript's README notes only that a paper "used v1 with an OCaml-syntax parser and heavily modified type checker", an implementation detail rather than an overall design influence.
research.reopenWhen: MLscript's own documentation states OCaml as an overall design influence.

research.note: The Gaea authors' ICMAS-96 paper describes Gaea as a logic programming language with "Prolog-like backward chain reasoning" but does not declare it a superset of Prolog; the superset claim appears only on PLDB.
research.reopenWhen: A primary source states Gaea is a superset/extension of Prolog.

research.note: The Progol page describes an ILP system that "allows arbitrary Prolog programs as background knowledge"; it does not state that Progol is a superset of the Prolog language.
research.reopenWhen: A primary source states Progol is a superset of the Prolog language.

research.note: Chapel's official overview paper lists its primary influences (C, Modula, Fortran, C++, Java, C#, CLU, Scala, ML, Perl, Matlab) and does not include Python.
research.reopenWhen: A primary Chapel source lists Python as a design influence or the influence list is materially revised.

research.note: Official Mojo material supports Python interoperability and compatibility, not a sufficiently explicit design-influence claim.
research.reopenWhen: An official Mojo design history or specification explicitly names Python as a design source for a concrete feature.

research.note: Official Mojo material supports Python interoperability and compatibility, not a sufficiently explicit design-influence claim.
research.reopenWhen: An official Mojo design history or specification explicitly names Python as a design source for a concrete feature.

research.note: Morloc README/docs present cross-language interoperability as the goal and do not state Python as a design-influence source.
research.reopenWhen: Morloc primary documentation states a Python design influence.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no Python design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states Python as an overall design influence.

research.note: Scroll's site presents the language for scientific writing and lists no design influences; the PLDB list mixes related notation/technology rather than design sources.
research.reopenWhen: Scroll's own documentation states Python as an overall design influence.

research.note: Speedie documentation only compares against Python (expressiveness) and notes one borrowed syntax form; it does not state Python as an overall design source.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states Python as an overall design influence.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no R design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states R as an overall design influence.

research.note: Jule's mission page describes an immutable-by-default model 'similar to Rust' as a comparison and states Jule is not functional; it does not declare Rust as a design-influence source.
research.reopenWhen: Jule primary documentation states Rust as a design influence rather than a similarity comparison.

research.note: The MLscript README frames the language around type inference, soundness, and pattern matching and does not state Rust as a design-influence source.
research.reopenWhen: MLscript primary documentation states Rust as a design influence.

research.note: Lil's documentation lists APL, J, K and Q as vector-oriented influences and describes its query syntax as only resembling SQL.
research.reopenWhen: Lil's own documentation states SQL as an overall design influence.

research.note: The Particles project page is a minimal index and states no SQL design influence.
research.reopenWhen: Particles' own documentation states SQL as an overall design influence.

research.note: The IBM SEQUEL 2 paper identity is present, but the batch could not obtain a stable readable primary copy that directly supports the SQL endpoint claim; the PLDB field remains unupgraded.
research.reopenWhen: A stable IBM paper copy or fixed archival source explicitly connects SQL to the specific SEQUEL 2 version.

research.note: The SQUARE data sublanguage (Boyce & Chamberlin, 1973) predates SEQUEL/SQL, and the IBM Research entries read do not state that SQUARE was influenced by SQL; the recorded direction is chronologically reversed.
research.reopenWhen: A primary source supports SQL influencing SQUARE, or the edge is corrected to SQUARE → SQL with a qualifying source.

research.note: TQL's page compares itself to SQL (plain-text vs binary databases) but states no SQL design influence.
research.reopenWhen: TQL's own documentation states SQL as an overall design influence.

research.note: AssemblyScript official homepage says TypeScript-like and highlights similarity, but this batch found no explicit design-source statement sufficient to upgrade the field relation.
research.reopenWhen: An official AssemblyScript design history or fixed source explicitly names TypeScript as a design input for concrete features.

research.note: Speedie's README lists its influences and does not name Visual Basic as a design source.
research.reopenWhen: Speedie's own documentation states Visual Basic as an overall design influence.

research.note: Author papers state 'Concurrent C (C++) is a parallel superset of C (C++)', but no hashable full-text copy of the Real-Time Concurrent C paper or the 'Implementing Concurrent C' paper could be secured for the review record.
research.reopenWhen: A hashable primary copy (paper PDF or abstract page) stating Real-Time Concurrent C's superset relation to C++ is obtained.

research.note: Deesel was a Java-based metaprogramming language described in encyclopedic sources as "nearly a superset of Java", but its official site is defunct (the archived domain shows a parked/for-sale page), so no hashable primary statement was secured.
research.reopenWhen: A hashable primary Deesel/G page or paper stating the superset relation to Java is obtained.

research.note: The current Objective-J/Cappuccino official entry point was not stably retrievable; the existing field is not upgraded from a third-party summary.
research.reopenWhen: A stable official Objective-J source or fixed repository revision is available.

research.reopenWhen: A hashable Slash language primary source (project site, docs or paper) is obtained.
